ORAL ORDER
This writ petition is filed by the petitioners herein assailing the order dated 04.12.2024 in Writ Petition No.19400/2024 (Annexure - G) passed by this Court.

2. Heard Sri. T.P. Vivekananda, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners, Sri. Yogesh D. Naik,
learned Additional Government Advocate for respondent No.1 - State, Sri. Vasanth, learned counsel appearing for respondent Nos.2 and 3 - KIADB and Sri. D.S. Jayaraj, learned counsel for respondent No.10.
3.

Sri. T.P. Vivekananda, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners contended that the respondent No.10 herein has preferred NC: 2026:KHC:12582 HC-KAR W.P.No.19400/2024,
without arraying the petitioners in the present writ petition as the parties and further, submitted that the claim made by respondent No.10 herein in W.P.No.19400/2024 pertains to the subject matter of the property in O.S.No.542/2021 on the file of Senior Civil Judge, Nelamangala
in which,

respondent No.10 is claiming right over the property in question and further claim of the respondent No.10 which has been already rejected by the competent revenue Court in the proceedings under Section 77A of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961 and in that view of the matter, it is contended that respondent No.10 has preferred W.P.No.19400/2024 seeking relief as not to release or disburse the compensation amount to anyone in view of acquisition of item No.2 of the schedule property therein and therefore, learned counsel submitted that, it is a clear abuse of process of law by respondent No.10 and accordingly, sought for interference of this Court.
NC: 2026:KHC:12582 HC-KAR 4.

Per contra, Sri. D.S. Jayaraj, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.10 submitted that respondent No.10 has preferred O.S.No.542/2021 seeking relief of partition and separate possession in respect of the subject matter of the properties mentioned in the suit schedule properties.
It is further submitted that the subject matter in the writ petition is also one of the suit properties in the suit.
Therefore, in the event, if the release of the compensation is made by the respondent Nos.2 and 3 namely, KIADB, irreparable loss would be caused to respondent No.10.

Hence, learned counsel sought to justify the impugned order dated 04.12.2024 in W.P.No.19400/2024 (Annexure - G).
5.

It is also submitted by learned counsel appearing for respondent No.10 that the petitioners herein have been impleaded in O.S.No.542/2021 and their impleading application came to be allowed on 22.01.2026.

sentences.text:
6. Having heard the learned counsels for the parties, I am of the opinion that as the petitioners herein NC: 2026:KHC:12582 HC-KAR in the present writ petition seeking rights over the properties in question, as per the proceedings in LRF (NML)184/98-99 and LRF (GRG) 8/99-2000 (Annexure - D), the order dated 04.12.2024 passed by this Court at Annexure - G requires to be set aside and W.P.No.19400/2024 has to be restored to file.
6.

In that view of the matter, taking into consideration the arguments advanced by the learned counsel appearing for petitioners as well as the contesting respondents herein, who are parties to the suit in O.S.No.542/2021, I find force in the submissions made by the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners that the order dated 04.12.2024 in W.P.No.19400/2024 is required to be recalled.

Accordingly, I pass the following;
 ORDER  i) Writ Petition is allowed.
ii) Order dated 04.12.2024 in Writ Petition No.19400/2024 is hereby set aside and NC:
2026:KHC:12582 HC-KAR Writ Petition No.19400/2024 is restored on file.
iii) It is open for the petitioners herein to implead in Writ Petition No.19400/2024, if so desires.

SD/-
(E.S.INDIRESH) JUDGE KLV List No.: 1 Sl No.: 48 C Krishnaiah vs The State Of Karnataka on 2 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70970459/
